author: Mark Atwood
text: API contract risk (supplement pass #2): MEDIUM — 2 new findings on top of the prior 15. The single most consequential addition is JMAP-ic0j.68 (P1 leakage), which raises the impact ceiling above the prior supplement's high-water mark: ~12 sites in calendars-server alone (and ~100 across the 7 extension-server siblings workspace-wide) hand-roll the leaky pattern `json!({"type":"serverFail", "description": e.to_string()})` in /set per-id maps. The principal.rs:121 fix (.53) covered only the top-level JmapError path; the per-id Value path has no analog helper, so the JMAP-jfia.20 backend-Display redaction contract is silently bypassed at every /set Other arm. The other new finding (JMAP-ic0j.69, P3 opinion) is a within-crate seed_object signature divergence — paper cut, no security implication. Risk classification unchanged at MEDIUM because (a) the most-consequential finding has a clear single-helper fix and (b) the per-id path was always intentional plain JSON, not a public API surface, so propagation across siblings is mechanical.
